sentences.en: Today, we have finally arrived at the lucky last in our birth order series.

sentences.en: If you've been tuned in for a while, over the last six months, I would say we've done like a dedicated episode for every sibling in the family.
sentences.zh: 如果你关注了一段时间，在过去的六个月里，我想我们为家庭中的每一个排行都做了一期专属节目。

sentences.en: So eldest, middle, youngeSt.

sentences.en: And in my last birth order episode, I said the youngest child would be the last episode we would do.
sentences.zh: 而在我的上一期出生顺序节目中，我说过最小的孩子将是我们做的最后一期节目。

sentences.en: And boy, oh boy, did I hear your outrage.
sentences.zh: 天哪，我的天哪，我可真是听到了你们的愤怒。

sentences.en: I heard and got so many DMs from you all and emails demanding that I do an episode on the youngest child.
sentences.zh: 我听到了你们的声音，收到了你们所有人发来的无数私信和电子邮件，强烈要求我做一个关于最小孩子的节目。

sentences.en: And my friends, I'm so sorry that I forgot about you, but I have listened and I got my research into gear to deliver you the episode you all wanted so much.
sentences.zh: 我的朋友们，很抱歉我把你们给忘了，但我已经听到了大家的呼声，并开足马力做好了调研，来为你们呈现这期大家心心念念的节目。

sentences.en: So for all of you who messaged me asking for this, I promise I did not forget.
sentences.zh: 所以对于所有给我发信息要求做这个主题的朋友们，我保证我没有忘。

sentences.en: The Only Child is just so special that they needed their own dedicated week and dedicated episode.
sentences.zh: 独生子女实在是太特别了，以至于他们需要有自己专属的一周和专属的一期节目。

sentences.en: And here it is.
sentences.zh: 而现在它来了。

sentences.en: This is it.
sentences.zh: 就是这个。

sentences.en: With the amount of families, I think choosing to have only one child in this day and age, honestly, we need to talk about it more, right?
sentences.zh: 考虑到如今年代选择只生一个孩子的家庭数量，说实话，我们真的需要多聊聊这个话题，对吧？

sentences.en: Because the research is getting more and more interesting by the day and more subjects are becoming available and Only Children are becoming so much more common.
sentences.zh: 因为研究日渐深入，变得越来越有趣，可供研究的对象也越来越多，独生子女也变得越来越普遍。

sentences.en: We've also had an entire country where they basically did an experiment on only children, as in like you think about China's one child policy.
sentences.zh: 我们还经历过一个国家，他们基本上对独生子女做了一场实验，就像你想想中国的独生子女政策一样。

sentences.en: They were like this perfect experimental condition where so many people obviously only had one child.
sentences.zh: 他们就像是那种完美的实验条件，因为显而易见有那么多人只生了一个孩子。

sentences.en: And it's this rare opportunity to really see how this experience of growing up, you know, as the only child, as the only child in the family normally
sentences.zh: 这是一个难得的机会，可以真正了解这种成长经历，你知道的，作为一个独生子女，作为家里唯一的孩子，通常

sentences.en: with the full attention of your two parents does impact your personality.
sentences.zh: 在拥有父母双方全神贯注的关注下，是如何影响你的个性的。

sentences.en: I also want to discuss some of the stereotypes about only children, the longstanding stereotypes and how they are actually deeply incorrect and why they have come to be.
sentences.zh: 我还想讨论一些关于独生子女的刻板印象，那些存在已久的刻板印象，它们实际上错得有多离谱，以及它们是如何形成的。

sentences.en: We're also going to discuss only child and parent dynamics, the pressure of needing to take care of your parents as you get older, parentification,
sentences.zh: 我们还将探讨独生子女与父母的动态关系、随着年龄增长需要照顾父母的压力、父母职化（家长式照顾），

sentences.en: also the different kinds of situations that may also impact the only child experience.
sentences.zh: 还有可能影响独生子女体验的各种不同情况。

sentences.en: So being the only child in a single person household, being the only child, but having step siblings, having lots of cousins.
sentences.zh: 比如在单亲家庭中是独生子女，是独生子女但有继兄弟姐妹，有很多堂表亲。

sentences.en: There's so many ways this can go.
sentences.zh: 这种情况有很多种发展可能。

sentences.en: We're going to hopefully tackle every single one of them.
sentences.zh: 我们希望逐一应对每一个情况。

sentences.en: You know, I don't like to ramble too much at the beginning of these birth order episodes because I always end up spoiling some of the best parts in like the first five minutes.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我不太喜欢在这些出生顺序节目的开头长篇大论，因为我总是会在前五分钟左右就不小心剧透了一些最精彩的部分。

sentences.en: So I'm not going to do that here.
sentences.zh: 所以我在这里就不这么做了。

sentences.en: I'm going to let the psychology and the research speak for itself.
sentences.zh: 我要让心理学和研究结果自己说话。

sentences.en: So without further ado, let's break down the unique and fascinating psychology of only children.
sentences.zh: 废话不多说，让我们来剖析独生子女独特而迷人的心理学。

sentences.en: So let's do a quick recap of birth order theory, the argument for it, but also against it.
sentences.zh: 那么让我们快速回顾一下出生顺序理论，支持它的论点，以及反对它的论点。

sentences.en: If you are a loyal listener and you have kept up to date with the whole series, firstly, thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 如果你是一个忠实听众，并且一直紧跟整个系列，首先，非常感谢。

sentences.en: But secondly, this might sound just a wee bit repetitive because we have spoken about it a little bit.
sentences.zh: 但其次，这听起来可能会有一点点重复，因为我们之前已经稍微聊过一点了。

sentences.en: But feel free to jump ahead like five to seven minutes to where we get into the juicy stuff.
sentences.zh: 不过大家可以随意快进大约五到七分钟，直接跳到我们进入精彩干货的部分。

sentences.en: But for those of you who don't know what birth order theory is, basically, it is a major theory on human personality.
sentences.zh: 但对于那些不知道什么是出生顺序理论的人来说，基本上，它是关于人类个性的一大主流理论。

sentences.en: Now, personality, we typically think of it as being shaped by two things, nature and nurture.
sentences.zh: 现在谈到个性，我们通常认为它由两件事塑造：先天和后天。

sentences.en: So we are obviously a product of genetics, but we are also a product of parenting style and food and country of birth and so many things.
sentences.zh: 所以我们显然是遗传的产物，但我们也是育儿方式、食物、出生国家以及诸多事物的产物。

sentences.en: But essentially, all the things that scientists and researchers believe impact our personality can either be from our environment or from our nature.
sentences.zh: 但从本质上讲，科学家和研究人员认为影响我们个性的所有因素，要么来自我们的环境，要么来自我们的先天。

sentences.en: So our genetic blueprint, who we were born to be.
sentences.zh: 也就是我们的基因蓝图，我们生来注定成为什么样的人。

sentences.en: Now, the position we are born into in a family and whether we have siblings or not, that is part of our environment and it falls into the nurture category.
sentences.zh: 现在，我们在家庭中出生的位置，以及我们是否有兄弟姐妹，这属于我们的环境，并落入后天范畴。

sentences.en: It influences our personality because of how it impacts how we are raised and experience the world as children, which leaves an impression
sentences.zh: 它之所以影响我们的个性，是因为它影响了我们在童年时期如何被抚养以及如何体验世界，从而留下了印记

sentences.en: and impact that carries on into adulthood.
sentences.zh: 和影响，并一直延续到成年期。

sentences.en: The thing that really defines the only child experience is that they don't obviously have siblings.
sentences.zh: 真正定义独生子女经历的是，他们显然没有兄弟姐妹。

sentences.en: It's their, I guess, solitude, isolation, their singularity.
sentences.zh: 这就是他们的，我猜是孤独、孤立以及他们的独特性。

sentences.en: That is the thing that is the kind of point of fascination for a lot of researchers.
sentences.zh: 正是这一点，成为了许多研究人员着迷的焦点。

sentences.en: It is just them.
sentences.zh: 世界只有他们自己。

sentences.en: And so our examination of what might influence the personality of an only child comes down to the absence of siblings rather than the presence of siblings as it does for eldest,
sentences.zh: 因此，我们对可能影响独生子女个性的因素的探究，归结为兄弟姐妹的缺席，而不是像老大、老二和老小那样由于兄弟姐妹的存在而产生的影响。

sentences.en: middle and youngest children.
sentences.zh: 老二和老小。

sentences.en: So back to this theory, the man who developed birth order theory was a man named Alfred Adler and he was known for a lot of things in his time.
sentences.zh: 所以回到这个理论，发展出出生顺序理论的人名叫阿尔弗雷德·阿德勒，他在当时以很多成就闻名。

sentences.en: You may have heard of him because of the inferiority complex.
sentences.zh: 你可能因为自卑情结听说过他。

sentences.en: That's one of the other famous ones.
sentences.zh: 那是他另一个著名的概念。

sentences.en: He was very busy during the mid-1900s, but birth order theory is probably what he's most well known for.
sentences.zh: 他在20世纪中期非常活跃，但出生顺序理论可能是他最广为人知的成就。

sentences.en: And again, it basically says that being the oldest, youngest, middle or only child will affect what characteristics and traits you develop over time, both when you are a child,
sentences.zh: 再次重申，它基本上指出，作为老大、老小、老二或独生子女，会影响你在成长过程中逐渐发展出什么样的特征和特质，无论是在你还是个孩子的时候，

sentences.en: when you're a teenager and as an adult.
sentences.zh: 还是在你十几岁时以及作为成年人时。

sentences.en: Let's be very, very clear.
sentences.zh: 让我们非常非常明确一点。

sentences.en: Birth order theory is not a medical prescription.
sentences.zh: 出生顺序理论不是医学处方。

sentences.en: It is not going to offer you any kind of psychological diagnosis.
sentences.zh: 它不会为你提供任何形式的心理学诊断。

sentences.en: It is a theory and a theory with gaps at that, with exceptions, with flaws, like any other theory.
sentences.zh: 它是一个理论，而且是一个存在漏洞的理论，有着例外和缺陷，就像任何其他理论一样。

sentences.en: And, you know, large scientific studies on this theory are really difficult to conduct.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，关于这个理论的大型科学研究确实很难进行。

sentences.en: One did take place in 2015 and it did find that it's very hard to get a diverse enough amount of people or to get enough people who want to participate
sentences.zh: 2015年确实进行过一项研究，结果发现很难招募到足够多元化的人群，或者招募到足够多愿意参与的人

sentences.en: to really sometimes draw conclusions.
sentences.zh: 来真正得出结论。

sentences.en: And so we do need to be careful about pigeonholing people purely based on the position in the family they were born in and whether or not they have siblings.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们确实需要谨慎，不能仅仅根据他们出生的家庭位置以及是否有兄弟姐妹，就把人死板地套入固定的类别中。

sentences.en: I think that's worth noting at the top of the episode, you're going to hear a lot of ideas today.
sentences.zh: 我认为在节目开头指出这一点很值得，你今天会听到很多观点。

sentences.en: They are not strict ideas.
sentences.zh: 它们并不是绝对死板的观点。

sentences.en: They do not determine exactly the person you are.
sentences.zh: 它们并不能完全决定你是一个什么样的人。

sentences.en: In my mind, discussing birth order theory really fills the same role as talking about personality tests.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，讨论出生顺序理论所起到的作用，其实和谈论性格测试是一样的。

sentences.en: They're really fun, they're useful and they do provide a structure or guide for better understanding where we sit in relation to others.
sentences.zh: 它们真的很有趣，很有用，并且确实提供了一个结构或指南，让我们更好地理解自己在与他人关系中的位置。

sentences.en: And they do help us better understand the traits within ourselves and the things that we may not have considered about the way we are.
sentences.zh: 它们确实帮助我们更好地理解我们内心的特质，以及我们可能没有考虑过的关于我们自身的生活方式。

sentences.en: But taking a personality test and then saying, well, that's everything
sentences.zh: 但是参加完一个性格测试，然后说，好吧，这就是我

sentences.en: I'm ever going to be is not the healthiest thing.
sentences.zh: 这辈子所有的样子了，可不是什么最健康的做法。

sentences.en: Neither is listening to an episode like this and saying, okay, well,
sentences.zh: 收听像这样的节目然后说，好吧，

sentences.en: I'm an only child, so this is my destiny.
sentences.zh: 我是个独生子女，所以这就是我的命运，也同样如此。

sentences.en: I always want to be somewhat cautious when discussing birth order theory because it does exist in a much larger ecosystem of factors, ideas, events, situations that impact
sentences.zh: 在讨论出生顺序理论时，我总是想保持一定的谨慎，因为它确实存在于一个更宏大的生态系统中，其中包含着影响我们为什么会成为这样的人的各种因素、观点、事件和情况。

sentences.en: why we are the way we are.
sentences.zh: 为什么我们是我们现在这样。

sentences.en: In my personal experience though, I am the eldest child,
sentences.zh: 不过就我个人经验而言，我是家里最大的孩子，

sentences.en: I'm the eldest daughter and I have found that a lot of what people say about me as an oldest child does really apply and a lot of what people say about my middle sister
sentences.zh: 我是长女，我发现人们对作为长女的我的许多看法确实很适用，而人们对我的中间妹妹

sentences.en: and my younger sister also really apply.
sentences.zh: 和我的小妹妹的许多看法也确实很适用。

sentences.en: So anecdotally, I do tend to believe some of the theory's propositions.
sentences.zh: 所以从经验来看，我确实倾向于相信该理论的一些主张。

sentences.en: But let's now turn to the star of the show, the only child.
sentences.zh: 但现在让我们把目光转向节目的主角，独生子女。

sentences.en: Let's start by talking about the stereotypes of what pop culture would have to say about only children and how they're routinely depicted.
sentences.zh: 让我们从流行文化对独生子女的看法以及他们通常是如何被描绘的刻板印象开始谈起。

sentences.en: The portrayed or expected traits of an only child that you might commonly hear about are typically based on the fact that they are the only child in the house.
sentences.zh: 你可能经常听到的关于独生子女被描绘或预期的特质，通常基于这样一个事实：他们是家里唯一的孩子。

sentences.en: Because of their family dynamic or structure, only children typically spend
sentences.zh: 由于他们的家庭动态或结构，独生子女通常

sentences.en: A, more time alone and second to that be more time in the company of adults compared to someone with siblings.
sentences.zh: A，花更多时间独自一人；其次B，与有兄弟姐妹的人相比，他们花更多时间与成年人相处。
